input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file content on `"
"` only (`text.split("
")`), without stripping ``. Windows-based tools (like the new accounting export tool finance started using) emit CRLF line endings, so each line (including the header) ends with a trailing ``. That extra character gets counted as part of the last column, causing the column-count check to fail and throw `errors.rowShape` on row 1. The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip `` or split on `/
|
/`) before parsing.

text: This confirms the likely bug: the parser splits on `"\n"` only, so Windows CRLF line endings leave a trailing `\r` in the header/columns, causing a column count mismatch.
